evidence: PlaceOrderUseCase.ts: private mapToDto(order: Order): OrderDto { return { id: order.id, status: order.getStatus(), lines: order.lines, createdAt: order.createdAt.toISOString() }; }
CancelOrderUseCase.ts execute(): repeats the same inline literal { id: order.id, status: order.getStatus(), lines: order.lines, createdAt: order.createdAt.toISOString() }
ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.ts execute(): orders.map(order => ({ id: order.id, status: order.getStatus(), lines: order.lines, createdAt: order.createdAt.toISOString() }))
UpdateOrderStatusUseCase.ts execute(): repeats the same inline OrderDto literal

UpdateOrderStatusUseCase.ts: const validStatuses: OrderStatus[] = ['placed', 'paid', 'packed', 'shipped', 'delivered']; repeats the OrderStatus/transition rules that belong to Order.transitionTo, and has no 'cancelled' entry
CancelOrderUseCase.ts and UpdateOrderStatusUseCase.ts both contain: if (!order) { throw new Error(`Order ${orderId} not found`); }
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The five use cases do share one concern: order and stock workflows that sit behind OrderController. The unit still fails the rubric because the same rules are copied into several files instead of living in one place.

First, the mapping from an Order to an OrderDto ({id, status: getStatus(), lines, createdAt: toISOString()}) is written out four separate times. PlaceOrderUseCase puts it in a private mapToDto method, so no other use case can reuse it. CancelOrderUseCase, ListOrdersByStatusUseCase and UpdateOrderStatusUseCase each repeat it inline. If the DTO shape changes, all four copies have to be updated and kept in sync.

Second, UpdateOrderStatusUseCase hard-codes its own validStatuses list. That list repeats the OrderStatus type and the transition rules that Order.transitionTo is meant to own. The application layer ends up holding a domain rule, and the list seems to have drifted already: it has no 'cancelled' entry, even though CancelOrderUseCase relies on order.canBeCancelled(). This is a likely sign of drift, but I can't confirm it from this unit alone.

The "Order X not found" lookup-and-throw is also repeated in CancelOrderUseCase and UpdateOrderStatusUseCase. That one is minor.
